clue.text: Where strikers are lined up to fight after game

indicators.note: after says the word for fighting follows the word for a game

parts.note: a match is a game, as in a football match
to box is to fight with the fists

explanation.surface: Football forwards line up, ready to scrap once the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' looks like footballers; here they are matches, which strike to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches, which are struck to light, sit in rows inside the small cardboard container.

clue.text: Sort of red spy man shortly arrests

indicators.note: arrests means holds, so the shortened man surrounds the spy
shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: man taken as written, then trimmed
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A communist spy is caught by a short man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of red' hints at politics but is a colour; 'shortly' trims MAN to MA, which then holds AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-crimson shade, so one variety of red.

clue.text: Shy victim I disbelieved in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nervous victim whom the speaker did not believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone lacking confidence and easily frightened.

clue.text: Admire the great man, or horsewhip viciously?

indicators.note: viciously suggests savage, wild treatment, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Should you idolise the great man, or beat him savagely?
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to venerate them like a figure of legend.

clue.text: Reproved, going after golden flower

indicators.note: going after says the word for reproved is placed behind the word for golden

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold

explanation.surface: A golden bloom, scolded and pursued.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is an exotic bloom of a large family of plants.

clue.text: Fancy wife goes with that man

parts.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: An attractive wife goes out with another man.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a sudden passing desire or impulse.

clue.text: Greeting husband, unwell

parts.note: ailing means sick

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a husband who is ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling out to someone to attract attention or welcome them.

clue.text: Headgear thrown at first in mud

indicators.note: in says the first letter goes inside the word for mud

parts.note: mire is deep mud or a bog

indicators.note: at first picks out the opening letter of thrown

explanation.surface: A hat gets thrown into the mud at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed ceremonial hat.

clue.text: Computer player is more spirited

definitions.meaning: game means plucky or willing, so more game is the comparative

explanation.surface: A video-game fan is described as having more pluck.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of video games is a gamer; and game meaning plucky gives the comparative form.

clue.text: Small room with first musician

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
1st, written out with the digit read as I, gives IST

explanation.surface: A tiny room where a leading performer lives.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written 1ST, and the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, so is one kind of instrumental performer.

clue.text: Criminal trio elected — would have failed this test?

definitions.text: Criminal trio elected — would have failed this test?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three crooks won office; a test of honesty would have caught them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both anagram and definition: crooked politicians would be caught by a polygraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A polygraph measures stress responses to check whether someone is telling the truth.

clue.text: Turning, lecturer is to indicate agreement

indicators.note: turning says the word for the lecturer is read backwards

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A lecturer turns round to show he agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping the head briefly is the usual gesture for saying yes.

clue.text: Small fib about some number that's marked on the road

indicators.note: about says the fib's letters go around the number

parts.note: a white lie is a harmless little untruth
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A minor untruth about a figure painted on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted stripes on a carriageway separate lanes or mark where to stop.

clue.text: Strongly desire extravagant praise

indicators.note: extravagant suggests something wild and unrestrained, so the letters of praise are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be lavishly complimented.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's hopes on reaching a goal.

clue.text: Poster to position shortly over a road

indicators.note: over says, in a down clue, the first part sits above the rest
shortly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to place is to put in position

explanation.surface: A sign to be put up briefly over a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a printed sign or notice displayed in public.

clue.text: Church employee right on the edge

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the letter for right follows the edge

parts.note: a verge is an edge or border, such as a grass strip beside a road

explanation.surface: A church worker is properly on the brink of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger looks after a church building and acts as an attendant at services.

clue.text: Country run — nothing taken with huge enthusiasm

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O looks like zero, nothing
a mania is a craze or obsessive enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A nation where running is met with wild enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Put down "Time to pay membership fee"

parts.note: a sub, short for subscription, is a club membership payment
due means owed now

explanation.surface: A curt note dismissing a reminder that the club fee is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a revolt is to crush or quell it.

clue.text: Children's theatre?

parts.note: not a stage for young audiences, but a little house children play in

explanation.surface: A query about a venue putting on shows for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a toy building where children act out make-believe, so it is their stage.

clue.text: Might war prisoner and monarch meet?

parts.note: POW stands for prisoner of war
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Could a captive and the king come face to face?
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun means strength or force.

clue.text: Stick in part of mouth

definitions.meaning: glue, or to fix with glue
the flesh in which the teeth are set

explanation.surface: Something lodged in a bit of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is called this, and so is the flesh holding the teeth.

clue.text: Good girl that can hold her drink

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A well-behaved young woman who can drink without getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold her drink' suggests tolerating alcohol; literally it is a vessel containing liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler or wine vessel literally contains a beverage.

clue.text: Speaker's fully absorbed, stuck into paper

indicators.note: a speaker's version is how the word sounds when said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: rapt means completely engrossed

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed while stuck into the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck into' reads as engrossed in reading; here it means enclosed in paper, like a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is enclosed in paper by being folded inside it.

clue.text: Mark time, and succeed holding area

indicators.note: holding means the word for succeed wraps around the letter for area

parts.note: to win is to succeed

explanation.surface: Note the time, and triumph while occupying a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb; it is the first name of the American writer Mark Twain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark is the first name of the author of Huckleberry Finn, with this surname.

clue.text: Travel using free energy

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid the house of mice
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Getting around by means of energy that costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to journey on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: State banks are failing

indicators.note: failing suggests collapse into disorder, so the letters of banks are get rearranged

explanation.surface: A financial news line: banks in the region are collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty US states, in the Great Plains.
